message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and the fundamentals supported a purchase: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% from $383.3B), operating income of $123.2B, net income of $93.7B, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3B — a business generating roughly $118B of annual operating cash against a $57.5B operating expense base, with Services growing 13% to $96.2B at a 73.9% gross margin and total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%. The main blemishes were a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid Decision (pushing the effective tax rate to 24.1% and net income down from $97.0B), an 8% decline in Greater China sales, and ongoing DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure — none of which change the underlying cash-generation story, and the company still returned $95.0B via buybacks plus $15.2B in dividends while holding $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 40 shares at $222.90 — about 0.1% above the market, well within "close to current market price" — which filled at $222.90 for a total of $8,916, satisfying the $10,000 per-order cap and leaving today's total purchases at $8,916 against the $20,000 daily limit; the order was a buy of an in-mandate ticker, funded entirely from the account's $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 222.90, 40 shares = $8,916. Under $10k per order, total today $8,916 < $20k. Cash was $50,000, so no money moved out.

Summary paragraph.
